title: The long way from
concrete to code.
intro.lede: I’m Razeen, a data engineer in Malaysia who started out as a civil engineer. I build systems, test ideas in public repos, and run long distances to keep my head straight.
intro.note: Told step by step and kept as a journal, so it grows as I do.

chapters.title: Engineer by training
body: Civil Engineering at Universiti Putra Malaysia. Four years of structures, soils and calculations that had to be right the first time. It taught me to respect systems long before I built software ones.

chapters.title: Registered, and restless
body: I registered as a Graduate Engineer with the Board of Engineers Malaysia and the Institution of Engineers Malaysia, and joined G&P Geotechnic. The engineering was real. So was the pile of repetitive work around it.

chapters.title: Automating the boring parts
body: I started writing Python and VBA to do the repetitive parts of geotechnical analysis for me, and cut a lot of manual effort. Somewhere in there I realised I cared more about the data than the drawings.

chapters.title: Making it official
body: I studied at night and turned the curiosity into credentials: Certified Data Analyst Associate, the PCEP Python certification, and Microsoft’s Power BI Data Analyst Associate.
chapters.credentialTitle: Microsoft Certified: Power BI Data Analyst Associate

chapters.title: Switching lanes
body: I left engineering for a Data Analyst role at EISmartwork, building models on datasets of more than ten million records and dashboards people actually used. At the same time I started a Master’s in Artificial Intelligence at UMPSA.

chapters.title: Master’s, and a microphone
body: I finished the Master’s in AI (CGPA 3.72). I was invited as a Google Speaker at AI Build 2025 and made the Top 20 of AWS National 2025 for training large language models.
At the Cursor × Anthropic hackathon we built LeadSightz, a sales-automation platform, in a weekend.

chapters.title: Data engineer, for real
body: At AEM Energy Solutions I build data pipelines and analytics for the energy sector. The problems there led to QualityPlus: a tool that scores data quality and turns the failures into a review workflow instead of a spreadsheet.

chapters.title: Same curiosity, different tracks
body: Sepang Vision Lab started as a question about how far public race data can go. Seventeen milestones later it’s a digital twin with replay, strategy simulation and an AI race engineer that is only allowed to explain the simulator.

chapters.title: Running, and the long game
body: Outside work I run road races. It’s the same loop as engineering: show up, measure, adjust, repeat. Progress you only notice over months.

outro: Input → process → iterate → progress. Still iterating.

principles.title: Input
principles.detail: Start from the real question and the data that actually exists, not the data I wish existed.

principles.title: Process
principles.detail: Build the smallest system that answers it end to end, then make each layer solid before adding the next.

principles.title: Iterate
principles.detail: Measure against a baseline. If the clever version doesn't beat the simple one, say so and try again.

principles.title: Progress
principles.detail: Ship, write down what I learned, and carry it into the next project. Or the next run.
